title: Unified SDK resilience patterns: backoff defaults, idempotency, and streaming edge cases
creator: Arielle Park
description: Produce a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) set of pragmatic defaults and guidance for retry/backoff policies, idempotency key usage patterns, and streaming ergonomics. Focus on developer ergonomics, predictable production behavior, and minimizing accidental double-processing for server-side at-most-once vs at-least-once semantics.
problem_statement: Current SDKs have divergent retry defaults, inconsistent idempotency guidance, and no documented streaming resume semantics. This causes customer confusion, production flakiness, accidental duplicate requests, and poor UX for partially-returned streaming responses.
proposal_summary: Ship a minimal, opinionated cross-SDK defaults package plus concrete examples for each language: (1) conservative retry policy default for non-idempotent write-like endpoints and permissive retry for safe read endpoints; (2) standardized idempotency-key semantics and helper utilities; (3) explicit streaming ergonomics with resume tokens, max-ttl, and partial-response invariants. Provide opt-out and per-endpoint override mechanisms.
design_notes: Avoid forcing strict semantics: defaults should prevent accidental retries for non-idempotent calls while making safe endpoints robust. Use header conventions (Idempotency-Key) and client helpers (generate_v4(), attach_if_missing()) rather than baked-in automatic key generation for all requests. For streaming, add a lightweight Resume-Token header and include explicit SDK helper to rehydrate partial state in client. Document trade-offs for at-most-once vs at-least-once and how backend retries relate to gateway/network retries.
language_examples: Python: Redwood SDK helper: session.request_with_retry(endpoint, method='POST', idempotency_key=maybe_generate(), retry_policy=RetryPolicy.conservative())
TypeScript: client.withRetry({policy: 'conservative', idempotencyKey: client.genIdemp()}) // returns Observable for streaming responses with 'resume' API
Go: client.Do(ctx, req, opts.WithIdempotencyKey(idemp), opts.WithBackoff(BackoffDefaultConservative)) // streaming: StreamClient.ReceiveWithResume(ctx, token)
default_retry_policy: Conservative defaults: initial_delay=200ms, max_delay=5s, factor=2.0, max_retries=3 for non-idempotent endpoints; for idempotent/safe endpoints default to max_retries=6 and max_delay=10s. Immediately fail on 4xx (except 429) and on explicit non-retryable error codes. Bubble server signaling for retryable vs non-retryable via x-rw-retryable header (true/false).
idempotency_guidance: Primary convention: clients MAY set Idempotency-Key for operations that create/modify server-side state. SDK helpers: (a) deterministic generator for user-provided stable keys (e.g., based on business id) and (b) random v4 generator for transient dedup use cases. Document when NOT to set a key (e.g., safe read ops). Servers MUST return 409 Conflict with existing resource metadata when a duplicate idempotency key is observed, or 200/201 with existing resource representation. Clients should treat 409 as non-retriable unless the response suggests stale state and an explicit retry-after header.
streaming_ergonomics: Streaming responses include meta frames: {type: 'progress'|'result'|'resume_token'}. SDKs expose an iterator/Observable plus a small resume API: resume(token) which requests `Range`-like resume from server. Resume tokens are short-lived (default 5 minutes) and opaque to clients. For best-effort partial results, SDK will: 1) surface intermediate text chunks immediately; 2) emit explicit 'stream_end' when final token received; 3) expose a boolean 'retriable' on stream error events indicating if resume is possible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec doc reviewed by SDK leads across languages; 2) Implemented helper functions in Python/TS/Go repos; 3) Cross-language integration tests that verify dedup using idempotency key, conservative retry prevents duplicate create, permissive retry recovers transient 5xx/429; 4) Streaming resume accepted by product and added to console docs; 5) Migration guidance published for existing customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge language SDK helpers behind feature flags; 2) Publish beta minor releases with migration docs; 3) Run dogfood test on internal workloads and Dedicated customers opt-in; 4) Flip defaults after 4 weeks if no regressions reported; 5) Add console toggle for 'aggressive retry' for power users.
testing_plan: Unit tests per language for backoff math and idempotency header behavior, integration tests with a simulated server that can deterministically inject failures and produce resume tokens, fuzz tests for random idempotency key collisions, and a small load test verifying duplicate suppression at the gateway tier.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental duplicate resources if idempotency misused. Mitigation: SDK warns when idempotency key is used with unsafe endpoints and logs a guidance link. Risk: resume token leakage. Mitigation: tokens are opaque, short-lived, and scoped to request IDs. Risk: inconsistent cross-SDK behavior. Mitigation: shared test harness and canonical fixtures used by all three language teams.
